faq.question: Is brunch popular in Paris?
faq.answer: Yes — brunch has become hugely popular in Paris, especially on weekends. Traditional French breakfast is light (coffee and croissant), so the more substantial Anglo-style brunch is a recent import. Most brunch spots are run by international or younger French chefs. Expect lines between 11am and 2pm on weekends.

faq.question: How much does brunch cost in Paris?
faq.answer: A la carte dishes typically cost EUR 12-22 per plate. Set menus or buffets range EUR 25-58 per person. HolyBelly's Savory Stack is around EUR 18. Budget spots like Paperboy keep plates under EUR 16.

faq.question: Do Paris brunch spots take reservations?
faq.answer: Most popular a la carte spots (HolyBelly, Kafkaf, Season) do NOT take reservations — first-come, first-served with 30-60 min weekend waits. Buffet brunches like La Bellevilloise and Le Repaire de Cartouche require reservations. Go on a weekday or arrive before 10am.

faq.question: What is the best brunch in Paris?
faq.answer: HolyBelly is the most recommended across Reddit, food blogs, and locals. Their Savory Stack (pancakes, fried eggs, bacon, bourbon butter) is iconic. For a French experience, Le Repaire de Cartouche offers oysters, foie gras, and rotisserie chicken.

faq.question: What arrondissement is best for brunch?
faq.answer: The 10th and 11th arrondissements have the highest concentration — HolyBelly, Kafkaf, The Hood, Le Repaire de Cartouche, Paperboy. The 3rd (Le Marais) is also excellent with Foufou, Season, and Ob-La-Di.

faq.question: When is the best time for brunch in Paris?
faq.answer: Weekdays 9-11am avoid lines. On weekends, arrive before 10am or after 3pm. Sunday is the busiest day — some spots have 45-60 min waits between 11am and 2:30pm.
